chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Indeed, the Imams in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are two kinds of Imams.
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: “And We made them Imams who guide by Our command.”
Not by the command of the people. They put the command of Allah before their own command, and the judgment of Allah before their own judgment.
And He said: “And We made them Imams who call to the Fire.”

They put their own command before the command of Allah, and their own judgment before the judgment of Allah, and they follow their desires in opposition to what is in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.أَمْرَ اللَّهِ: the command of Allah, which is given priority by true Imams
key_terms.إِمَامَانِ: two categories or kinds of Imams
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةَ: the leaders or Imams referred to in the Book of Allah
key_terms.بِأَمْرِنَا: by Our command, meaning through divine authority and direction
key_terms.بِأَهْوَائِهِمْ: by their desires, meaning personal whims opposed to revelation
key_terms.حُكْمَ اللَّهِ: the judgment of Allah, which true Imams place above personal judgment
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah, the standard against which leadership is measured
key_terms.يَدْعُونَ إِلَى النَّارِ: calling to the Fire, referring to misguiding leaders

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the two kinds of Imams mentioned in the Qur'an?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the Qur'an presents two kinds of leaders: Imams who guide by Allah’s command, and Imams who call to the Fire. The distinction lies in whether they prioritize Allah’s command and judgment or their own desires and decisions. It highlights true religious authority as submission to divine command rather than popular demand or personal inclination.
